sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Why was the Glorious Revolution of 1688 called 'glorious'? Why did King James II lose the support of his countrymen?
questions.answer: (1) It was called the Glorious Revolution because no blood was shed to achieve its success. (2) The Stuart king James II lost the popular support of his countrymen. This was due to his harsh attitude towards the people. The creation of an expensive standing army and increasing employment of Roman Catholics in the government, army and universities had angered the people. (3) The Parliament removed King James II from the throne in favor of his daughter Mary II and her husband William III, Prince of Orange. The autocratic rule of James II was replaced with a constitutional form of government.

questions.q: Why did Europeans want to trade with the East during the Industrial Revolution?
questions.answer: (1) These countries needed constant supply of raw materials and a ready market for selling the finished goods. The capitalists too needed new places and new industries to invest their surplus capital since these needs could not be fulfilled in their own countries or in neighboring areas. (2) This was because these countries were rich in resources but were politically and militarily weak and industrially backward. This one-sided trade was not profitable for European merchants so they started smuggling opium to China to demoralise the Chinese youth and exchange Chinese goods. Other countries of South East Asia also suffered under Imperialism. Since the war was spread over a very large part of the world for the first time, it is known as World War I.

or.answer: (1) He/she forms the Council of Ministers by advising the Governor and allocates and can change portfolios. sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Describe the condition of Italy on the eve of the Renaissance in the 14th century.
questions.answer: (1) Italy was divided into small city states at that time. Many of them were built on the ruins of ancient Roman buildings. (2) Moreover, the position of Italian cities such as Venice made them centers of trade and intellectual crossroads. (3) The new form of political and social organization gave political freedom and a suitable atmosphere for academic, artistic and cultural advancement. (4) Many great ideas, along with wealth, were brought by merchants from far corners of the globe. People had more leisure time for study and other activities.

questions.q: Explain any three consequences of the Second World War.
questions.answer: (1) It caused unprecedented loss of life, property and resources. The German Jews were either exterminated or sent to concentration camps. The Japanese cities of Hiroshima and Nagasaki were almost wiped off when atomic bombs were dropped on them. The danger of nuclear holocaust was one of the major consequences of the war. (2) Germany was divided into four zones and Japan was put under US supervision; imperialism weakened and colonies in Asia and Africa became independent. (3) The USA and USSR emerged as superpowers, the Cold War began, and the United Nations was founded.

questions.q: Describe any three factors affecting the climate of India.
questions.answer: (1) So in south of this latitude we find tropical climate and towards the north we find sub-tropical climate. For example, Andhra Pradesh would be hotter than Haryana. Broadly speaking parts lying south of the Tropic of Cancer receive more solar heat than those lying north of it. (2) Location:The places which are closer to equator have high temperature. Distance from the sea: The southern half of India is surrounded by sea from three sides: the Arabian Sea in the west, the Bay of Bengal in the east and the Indian Ocean in the south. For example the area of North India which is far away from the sea has extreme type of climate and the area of south India which is nearer to the sea has equable type of climate. In peninsular region, India’s rainfall decreases from coast to interior parts. (3) Mountains: the Himalayas block cold Central Asian winds and trap the monsoon; the Western Ghats cause heavy rain on their windward side. (Altitude, surface winds and jet streams also matter.)

questions.q: How is casteism a challenge to Indian democracy? Explain in three points.
questions.answer: (1) caste system is the practice of untouchability which is continuing in different covert and overt ways in spite of the constitutional ban imposed on it. (2) Casteism has become notorious as a strategy of exploitation of caste consciousness for narrow political gains. (3) There are enormous inequalities in our society which are posing serious challenge to Indian democracy.

or.q: How is criminalisation of politics a challenge to Indian democracy? Explain in three points.
or.answer: (1) Criminalization of politics is the very negation of democratic values. (2) There have been allegations that there are some elements in politics who do not have faith in democratic values and practices. (3) We, as awakened citizens and as voters of the largest democracy in the world, can also contribute by discouraging such persons who have a criminal background, from contesting elections. The citizens must respect the law and reject violence.

questions.q: Explain any three measures taken by the government for the economic and social empowerment of women.
questions.answer: (1) Since women comprise the majority of the population below the poverty line, poverty eradication programmes are specifically addressed to their needs and problems. In view of the critical role of women in the agriculture and allied sectors as producers, concentrated efforts are being made to ensure that benefits of training, extension and various programmes reach them in proportion to their numbers. This has played a central role in the process of enhancing women’s participation in public life. (2) Comprehensive support in terms of labour legislation, social security and other support services is provided to women to enable them to participate in various industrial sectors, especially electronics, information technology, food processing, agro industry and textiles. The provision of support services for women, like child care facilities, including crèches at work places and educational institutions, homes for the aged and the disabled are being improved to create an enabling environment and to ensure their full cooperation in social, political and economic life. (3) Equal access to education, health and nutrition and elimination of violence against women; politically, one-third reservation in local bodies.

or.q: What is the role of the National Rural Health Mission? Mention any two other health programmes for women and children.
or.answer: (1) Medical facilities are concentrated in cities, so NRHM was launched to provide accessible, affordable health care in rural areas, reducing the rural–urban gap. (2) Apart from NRHM, Government of India has also launched many programmes related to health of women and children like Janani Suraksha Yojna (JSY), Balika Samridhi Yojna (BSY), and Kishori Shakti Yojna (KSY).

questions.q: Explain the six Fundamental Rights guaranteed by the Indian Constitution.
questions.answer: (1) It has five provisions (Articles 14-18) to provide for equality before law or for the protection of law to all the persons in India and also to prohibit discrimination on the grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth. (i) Equality before Law: The Constitution guarantees that all citizens will be equal before law. (iv) Abolition of Untouchability: Practising untouchability in any form has been made a punishable offence under the law. (2) Right to Freedom (Art. 19–22): six freedoms, protection in conviction, life and personal liberty, safeguards on arrest; Article 21A gives free education to 6–14-year-olds. (3) The citizens have been guaranteed the right against exploitation through Articles 23 and 24 of the Constitution. Trafficking, especially of young women, girls and even boys is continuing as an illegal trade. This right aims at eliminating one of the most serious problems, child labour, that India has been facing since ages. Ten Fundamental Duties have been added in Part-IV of the Constitution under Art 51A in the year 1976 through the 42nd Constitutional Amendment. Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right to Freedom of Religion and Cultural and Educational Rights (6) Right to Constitutional Remedies (Art. 32): approach the Supreme Court if rights are violated.
